question.text: An electron is moving under the influence of the electric field of a uniformly charged infinite plane sheet <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> having surface charge density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>+</mo><mi>σ</mi></math>. The electron at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> is at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> and has a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The maximum value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>σ</mi></math>, if the electron strikes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi><mfenced close="]" open="["><mfrac><mrow><mi>m</mi><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mi>e</mi></mfrac></mfenced><mo> </mo><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> is _____.

solution.text:
The value of the electric field due to the uniformly charged plane sheet is given by

E=σ2ε0   ...1

Thus, the force on the electron is given by

F=-eE=-σe2ε0   ...2

So, the acceleration of the electron is given by

a=-σe2ε0 m

Given, u=1 m s-1, t=1 s and S=-1 m

Using the equation of motion, it can be written that

-1=1×1-12×σe2ε0 m×(1)2⇒σ=8ε0 me C m-2

∴α=8.
